name: organism-interaction
title: Organism Interaction
description: An interaction between two dwc:Organisms during a dwc:Event.
notes: Supports only primary observed interactions, not habitual or derived taxon-level interactions. Pairwise interactions must be used to represent multi-organism interactions. When possible, typify the action rather than the state from which an action is inferred, with the actor as the subject dwc:Occurrence and the acted-upon as the related dwc:Occurrence. Only one direction of a two-way interaction is necessary, though both are permissible as distinct OrganismInteractions with distinct subject dwc:Occurrences.
examples: `a bee visiting a flower`; `a Mallophora ruficauda hunting an Apis mellifera in flight`; `a viral infection in a plant`; `a female spider mating with a male spider`; `a lion cub nursing from its mother`; `a mosquito sucking blood from a chimpanzee's arm`; `a slug eating a fungus growing on decomposing stump (2 interactions)`

fields.name: organismInteraction_pk
fields.title: Organism Interaction (Primary Key)
fields.description: A unique identifier for a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to guarantee uniqueness.

fields.name: organismInteractionID
fields.title: Organism Interaction ID
fields.notes: The value in this field MUST be preserved in aggregation. Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: event_fk
fields.title: Event (Foreign Key)
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: organismInteractionDescription
fields.title: Organism Interaction Description
fields.description: A verbatim description of a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.examples: `Mallophora ruficauda capturing an Apis mellifera worker in flight.`

fields.name: subjectOccurrence_fk
fields.title: Subject Occurrence (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a subject dwc:Occurrence in a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: subjectOrganismPart
fields.title: Subject Organism Part
fields.description: An anatomical part of a subject dwc:Organism involved in a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: organismInteractionType
fields.title: Organism Interaction Type
fields.description: A category that best matches the nature of a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.
fields.examples: `visited flower of`; `pollinated by`; `parasitoid of`; `mated with`; `was attached to`

fields.name: relatedOccurrence_fk
fields.title: Related Occurrence (Foreign Key)
fields.description: An identifier for a related dwc:Occurrence in a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY be changed in aggregation to preserve the relationship to the related primary key.

fields.name: relatedOccurrenceID
fields.title: Related Occurrence ID
fields.description: An identifier for a related dwc:Occurrence in a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: The value in this field MAY refer to a dwc:Occurrence within or external to the dataset in which this record originated.

fields.name: externalRelatedOccurrenceID
fields.title: External Related Occurrence ID
fields.description: An identifier for a related dwc:Occurrence (the object) of a dwc:ResourceRelationship that is not within the same dataset.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a globally unique identifier.

fields.name: externalRelatedOccurrenceSource
fields.title: External Related Occurrence Source
fields.description: A reference to a source outside the dataset where the related dwc:Occurrence record can be found.

fields.name: relatedOrganismPart
fields.title: Related Organism Part
fields.description: An anatomical part of a object dwc:Organism involved in a dwc:OrganismInteraction.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to use a controlled vocabulary.

fields.name: feedbackURL
fields.title: Feedback URL
fields.description: A uniform resource locator (URL) that points to a webpage on which a form may be submitted to gather feedback about the record.
fields.notes: Recommended best practice is to optionally include query strings that act to pre-populate web page form elements and communicate the context.
